en.title: Octavian Lunar Calendar — Phase of Date
en.description:
An Octavian year is divided into months with the same lengths as the 12 months of the Earth Gregorian calendar (a fixed non-leap year), and there are 8 cyclic moon phases: NewMoon, Crescent, Quarter, Gibbous, Full, Waning, Eclipse, Twilight. Given the phase at the start of the year, a month, and a day of that month, find the phase on that date.

The input/output protocol and the explicitly marked site-supplemented constraints were compiled by CSWork.
en.input: One line with three fields: startPhase month day. startPhase is one of the 8 names above; 1≤month≤12, and day is within the valid range for that month.
en.output: Output the name of the moon phase on that date.
en.explanation: See the accompanying editorial for the full approach and proof.
